subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 1: New Media – Listening and Speaking
outcomes: Use journalism words like reporter, source and fake news.
Listen for key words and say the stressed syllable in words.
Give opinions and make suggestions with useful expressions.

tf.s: A journalist is a person who reports the news.
tf.why: Yes! Journalists research and report the news.

tf.s: In the interview, the journalist says journalism is faster than social media at reporting news.
tf.why: He says social media is often faster at spreading breaking news.

tf.s: Fake news is news that is not based on facts.
tf.why: Correct, so we must check the source.

tf.s: In 'online', the stress is on the second syllable.
Chart b shows printed newspaper sales going up and online readership going down.
tf.why: Chart b shows printed sales falling and online readership rising.
Well done, K means one thousand.

tf.s: 'I'm not sure about it' is a positive answer to a suggestion.
tf.why: It shows doubt; 'That sounds great' is positive.

tf.s: In the podcast, Mo has the most followers of the three teenagers.
'One example of this is…' is used to disagree.
tf.why: It is used to give an example.

tf.s: In 'participate', the first syllable is stressed.
tf.why: The stress is on the second syllable: par-TI-ci-pate.

boxes.q: News that is not based on facts is ...
boxes.why: Fake news is not true or not based on facts.

boxes.q: Which word completes: '___ don't we start a YouTube channel?'
How many followers does Rebecca have?

boxes.why: Peter feels successful by tweeting regularly.
Mo makes videos and has about 120K followers.

boxes.q: How can we check if news is real?
boxes.why: A trusted source helps us know the news is real.

boxes.q: Which is a polite way to disagree?
o: I'm sorry but I don't agree

boxes.q: Which word has the stress on the first syllable?
boxes.why: DI-gi-tal is stressed on the first syllable.

boxes.q: What does Jack suggest in the dialogue?
boxes.why: Jack suggests a YouTube channel to Dan.

hunt.q: A person who reports the news
A positive reply to a suggestion
A show you listen to online

mcq.q: What does 'trust' mean in 'We trust this news source'?
o: believe it is honest and true
mcq.why: We trust sources that give true information.

mcq.q: Which chart shows the trend in Listening 1.4?
mcq.why: Chart b shows printed sales falling and online readership rising.

mcq.q: According to Dr David, what can journalists do to compete with social media?
mcq.why: He also says they can use audio, video and social media.

mcq.q: Your friend says, 'How about making a school news podcast?' You like the idea. You say:
o: I'm sorry but I don't agree.

mcq.q: Complete: 'Online newspapers are better ___ I can read them anywhere.'
Which key words should you listen for in 'Anyone can be a journalist'?
mcq.why: Key words carry the main meaning of the statement.

mcq.q: Mo says you should create content you love. Why does this help?
o: Your passion shows and gives value to followers.
mcq.why: Followers enjoy content made with passion.

mcq.q: Why should you check the source of news on social media?
mcq.why: Checking sources helps us avoid fake news.
